QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_15

question.text: Sanjay invested Rs.50,000 which grew to Rs.70,000 over 40 months. What is the simple annualized return?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 152, the simple annualization factor is applied to the absolute return. Absolute return = (70,000 - 50,000)/50,000 x 100 = 40%. Simple annualized return = 40% x (12/40) = 12.00% per annum. The Trap: Candidates often report the absolute return (40%) or incorrectly divide by 40 months rather than converting 40 months into years (40/12 = 3.33 years). Note: Per page 153, CAGR accounts for compounding and is the accepted measure for periods over one year. The stem here explicitly asks for the simple annualized return, so the page 152 simple-annualization formula applies.
